title: CompTIA Linux+ Essentials
description: Test your Linux system administration knowledge for CompTIA Linux+ certification

questions.question: Which command is used to change file permissions in Linux?
questions.explanation: chmod (change mode) is used to modify file permissions. For example, 'chmod 755 file.txt' sets read, write, execute for owner, and read, execute for group and others.

questions.question: What does the command 'ls -la' do?
choices: Lists files in long format including hidden files
Lists files by last accessed time
questions.explanation: The 'ls -la' command lists all files (including hidden files starting with .) in long format, showing permissions, ownership, size, and modification date.

questions.question: Which directory contains user home directories in Linux?
questions.explanation: /home contains subdirectories for each regular user account. For example, user 'john' would have a home directory at /home/john. The root user's home is /root.

questions.question: What command displays the current working directory?
questions.explanation: pwd (print working directory) displays the full path of the current directory you are in.

questions.question: Which file contains user account information in Linux?
questions.explanation: /etc/passwd contains user account information including username, UID, GID, home directory, and default shell. Passwords are stored in /etc/shadow for security.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the sudo command?
questions.explanation: sudo (superuser do) allows permitted users to execute commands with the security privileges of another user, typically root, without logging in as root.

questions.question: Which command is used to search for files in Linux?
questions.explanation: The find command searches for files in a directory hierarchy based on various criteria like name, size, type, or modification time. Example: 'find /home -name '*.txt''.

questions.question: What does the command 'df -h' display?
choices: Disk space usage in human-readable format
questions.explanation: df -h (disk free) displays disk space usage for all mounted filesystems in human-readable format (using KB, MB, GB instead of blocks).

questions.question: Which command is used to view running processes?
questions.explanation: ps (process status) displays information about running processes. Common usage includes 'ps aux' to see all processes with detailed information.

questions.question: What is the default shell in most Linux distributions?
questions.explanation: bash (Bourne Again Shell) is the default shell in most Linux distributions, providing command-line interface and scripting capabilities.

questions.question: Which command is used to change a user's password?
questions.explanation: The passwd command is used to change user passwords. Running 'passwd' changes your own password, while 'passwd username' (as root) changes another user's password.

questions.question: What does the command 'tar -xzf file.tar.gz' do?
questions.explanation: tar -xzf extracts (x) a gzip-compressed (z) tar archive from a file (f). This is commonly used to unpack downloaded software packages.

questions.question: Which runlevel represents single-user mode in traditional init systems?
questions.explanation: Runlevel 1 is single-user mode, used for system maintenance and recovery. Runlevel 0 is halt, 3 is multi-user without GUI, and 5 is multi-user with GUI.

questions.question: What command is used to display the last few lines of a file?
questions.explanation: tail displays the last 10 lines of a file by default. You can specify a different number with -n, or use 'tail -f' to follow a file in real-time (useful for log files).

questions.question: Which command displays network interface configuration?
questions.explanation: ifconfig (interface configuration) displays or configures network interfaces. In modern systems, 'ip addr' or 'ip a' is preferred, but ifconfig is still widely used.
